title: Karna turns down a throne
hook: the peace talks are over, and Krishna invites Karna up into his chariot for a ride outside the city.
carry: keeping faith is dharma, even when it costs a crown
tomorrow: what does Karna give the mother who gave him away?

segments.voice: Yesterday Krishna made the whole case for peace before the Kuru court, and Duryodhana refused. Your line: dharma tries peace first, even expecting a no.

A chariot rolls out through the gates of Hastinapura. The embassy has failed. Duryodhana won't give the Pandavas their share, and war is coming. But before Krishna goes, he does something odd. He calls Karna, Duryodhana's friend and champion, up beside him, and the two ride out of the city together, away from the crowd. What Krishna says on that ride could stop the war before it starts, and it rests on a secret about who Karna's mother is.
screen: `THE EMBASSY HAS FAILED.` → `KRISHNA CALLS KARNA UP` → `A SECRET ON THE ROAD`

segments.voice: Here is the secret. Karna is Kunti's son, born to her before she married Pandu. That makes him, Krishna says, the eldest brother of the five Pandavas. Then comes the offer. Come with me. Your brothers will touch your feet. You will be king, and Yudhishthira himself will stand behind your throne. Karna's answer is the heart of today. He says he already knows. Then he says why it changes nothing. His mother set him adrift as a newborn. A charioteer named Adhiratha found him, and Adhiratha's wife Radha raised him. Her milk fed him and her love kept him alive, he says, and he will not stop being her son for a crown. He married among the charioteer's people, and he has children there. And for years Duryodhana has stood by him when no one else would. He gave Duryodhana his word, and he means to keep it. Then he asks Krishna for one thing: don't tell Yudhishthira. If Yudhishthira learned that Karna was his elder brother, he would hand him the kingdom, and Karna would hand it straight to Duryodhana. Better that it stays secret. So a man is offered everything he ever wanted, and turns it down for the people who loved him first. In Hindu teaching, gratitude, remembering who held you up, is part of dharma, and so is keeping your word. Karna holds to both. But he holds them on Duryodhana's side, and that's the knot. Many teachers say Karna is right by one duty and ruinous by another, and the epic honors him and grieves him at once.
screen: `KARNA IS KUNTI'S FIRST SON` · `THE OFFER: BROTHERS AND A THRONE` · `RADHA RAISED ME; I STAY HER SON` · then, large: `HE KEEPS FAITH, AND PAYS FOR IT`

segments.voice: Bring to mind someone who raised you, or stood by you when no one else did. Many Hindus honor that by touching the feet of parents and elders, a pranam. Breathing in, picture their face; breathing out, bow to them in your mind, or for real the next time you see them. If you don't pray, just thank them, silently or out loud.
Udyoga. The preparing, the getting ready for war: the book where every side makes its choices before the fighting begins. Today, Karna made his.
Your line: keeping faith is dharma, even when it costs a crown. Karna stayed Radha's son. Tomorrow: what does Karna give the mother who gave him away?

fork.reveal: Karna refuses. he names Radha, who raised him, and Duryodhana, who stood by him: gratitude and his word come first. then he asks Krishna to keep the secret.

original.note: the name of the Mahabharata's fifth book, the Udyoga Parva, the book of getting ready for war.

Krishna's offer is simplified ('Yudhishthira himself will stand behind your throne'); Ganguli's text has a longer list, including Draupadi; the script leaves that out deliberately.
